name: Beau Bayh
gradeNote: No public positions found on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns; did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates him 'Liberal' based on public data, and he is endorsed by Democrat Pete Buttigieg. His stated priorities are an independent audit of the office, protecting early voting, citizen-led ballot initiatives and ending straight-ticket voting.
description: Indianapolis attorney, former U.S. Marine Corps captain and son of former Gov. and Sen. Evan Bayh, nominated at the June 2026 Democratic convention.

name: Max Engling
gradeNote: On the iVoterGuide questionnaire he strongly agreed that life deserves legal protection from conception, that marriage is one man and one woman, and that no one should be compelled to provide services against religious beliefs; he also supports photo voter ID and signed the Americans for Tax Reform Taxpayer Protection Pledge. He has no voting record, and President Trump endorsed him in October 2026.
description: Former U.S. House Republican staffer and regional director for Sen. Jim Banks who defeated incumbent Diego Morales for the Republican nomination at the June 2026 convention.

name: Lauri A. Shillings
gradeNote: Her campaign focuses on cutting red tape, modernizing business filings, campaign-finance transparency and neutral election administration; she states no positions on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns. She did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her 'Moderate.'
description: Chair of the Hamilton County Libertarian Party and creative director at the University of Indianapolis, running as the Libertarian nominee.

name: Greg Ballard
gradeNote: As Indianapolis mayor in 2015 he publicly denounced Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act and urged lawmakers to add sexual orientation and gender identity to state civil rights protections. He did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates him 'Liberal' based on public data.
description: Former two-term Republican mayor of Indianapolis (2008-2015) and retired Marine lieutenant colonel, running as an independent on the Lincoln Party line.

name: Jessica Bailey
gradeNote: No public positions found on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns; she did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her 'Liberal' based on public data. On fiscal issues she opposes eliminating property and gas taxes, says she would not raise taxes without debate, and wants a more accessible state transparency portal.
description: Two-term Porter County Circuit Court clerk and former Portage Township school board member, running as the Democratic nominee.

name: Elise Nieshalla
gradeNote: In office she voted in March 2025 for a non-ESG investment policy for the state's Hoosier START retirement plan and chairs a state financial officers' national-debt task force. On the iVoterGuide questionnaire she supports protecting life from conception, one-man-one-woman marriage, constitutional carry, religious-conscience protections and parental rights; she is endorsed by the Indiana Republican Assembly.
description: Incumbent Republican comptroller appointed in 2023, former Boone County Council president and former Indiana Department of Commerce economic development manager.

name: John Schick
gradeNote: His only public positions found are from a 2022 interview: reduce government spending, cut regulations, and keep the auditor independent of the governing party. He did not answer the 2026 surveys from the Capital Chronicle or iVoterGuide, which rates him 'Insufficient Information.'
description: Chesterton business consultant and former Libertarian Party state treasurer, running his third or fourth campaign for comptroller/auditor.

name: Coumba Kebe
gradeNote: She questions whether Indiana's anti-ESG investment efforts served taxpayers, opposes eliminating property and gas taxes, and says government should not make decisions 'just focused on the numbers.' She did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her 'Liberal' based on public data; no positions were found on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns.
description: Health care executive and founder of Scope Consulting, which serves home care agencies, running as the Democratic nominee after losing a Democratic primary for Indiana House District 29.

name: Daniel Elliott
gradeNote: As treasurer he put BlackRock on an ESG watchlist in 2024 and, as an INPRS board member, voted to replace it as manager of a roughly $969 million portfolio. On the iVoterGuide questionnaire he supports defunding Planned Parenthood, opposes elective abortion except to save the mother's life, backs one-man-one-woman marriage, wants no new gun restrictions and supports religious-conscience protections and parental rights.
description: Incumbent Republican state treasurer first elected in 2022, former Morgan County Council member and software engineer/consultant.
